subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Discontinuous variation differs from continuous variation because it:
options: Is always caused by the environment
Falls into distinct, non-overlapping categories controlled by one or few genes
Shows a normal distribution
Cannot be inherited
questions.explain: Discontinuous variation gives discrete categories, typically controlled by one or a few genes with little environmental effect.

questions.q: Two genes are described as autosomally linked when they:
options: Code for the same protein
Always assort independently
Are located on the X chromosome
Are located close together on the same autosome and tend to be inherited together
questions.explain: Linked genes lie on the same (non-sex) chromosome and tend to be inherited together rather than assorting independently.

questions.q: In a classic predator-prey relationship, why does the predator population peak shortly after the prey population peaks?
options: Predators cause prey numbers to rise
Abundant prey allows more predators to survive and reproduce, with a time lag
Prey numbers never affect predator numbers
Predators reproduce before prey are available
questions.explain: A peak in prey provides plentiful food, so predator numbers rise afterwards, lagging behind the prey peak.

questions.q: What is the function of tRNA during translation?
options: To carry the genetic code from the nucleus to the ribosome
To unwind the DNA double helix
To bring specific amino acids to the ribosome according to its anticodon
To catalyse peptide bond formation
questions.explain: Each tRNA carries a specific amino acid and pairs its anticodon with the complementary mRNA codon.

Removing introns from pre-mRNA
Methylating cytosine bases to silence genes
Binding to a receptor to form a transcription factor complex that switches on target genes
questions.explain: Oestrogen binds its receptor, and the complex acts as a transcription factor that initiates transcription of target genes.

questions.q: Disruptive selection differs from the other types because it:
options: Favours the mean phenotype
Acts only on sex-linked genes
Reduces all variation
Favours both extreme phenotypes at the expense of intermediates
questions.explain: Disruptive selection favours both extremes and selects against intermediate phenotypes, potentially leading to two distinct groups.

questions.q: DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides to the 3' end of a strand. This explains why:
options: Both strands are synthesised continuously
Helicase is required to join the fragments
The leading strand is synthesised in fragments
The lagging strand is synthesised discontinuously as Okazaki fragments
questions.explain: Because synthesis must run 5' to 3', the antiparallel lagging strand is built discontinuously as Okazaki fragments later joined by ligase.

questions.q: A dihybrid cross between two double heterozygotes shows a phenotypic ratio significantly different from 9:3:3:1. This deviation is best explained by:
options: Random fertilisation
Codominance
A larger sample size
Autosomal linkage between the two genes
questions.explain: Linkage keeps parental allele combinations together, distorting the expected independent-assortment 9:3:3:1 ratio.

questions.q: Restriction endonucleases that leave 'sticky ends' are useful in recombinant DNA technology because:
options: They cut DNA into blunt fragments only
The single-stranded overhangs allow complementary fragments to anneal before ligation
They amplify DNA exponentially
They permanently join DNA without ligase
questions.explain: Sticky ends are short single-stranded overhangs that base-pair with complementary ends, allowing DNA ligase to join the fragments.

questions.q: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous parents (Tt x Tt), the expected phenotypic ratio is:
questions.explain: A heterozygous monohybrid cross gives a 3:1 ratio of dominant to recessive phenotypes.

questions.q: In the nitrogen cycle, which process converts atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia or ammonium ions?
options: Ammonification
Nitrogen fixation
Denitrification
Nitrification
questions.explain: Nitrogen fixation, carried out by bacteria such as Rhizobium and Azotobacter, converts N2 into ammonia.

questions.q: The Hardy-Weinberg principle predicts that allele and genotype frequencies remain constant only if:
options: Mating is non-random
There is no mutation, no selection, no migration, random mating and a large population
The population is small with frequent migration
Selection strongly favours one allele
questions.explain: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium assumes a large population with no mutation, selection or migration and random mating.
